summary.prose: This Story adds a dedicated 'Model Tiers' webview panel to the VS Code extension, replacing the hard-to-read flat settings list with one card per tier (core/mid/cheap) showing runner, model and effort dropdowns, cloud/local hosting badges, and an inline 'not supported'/'not listed'/'floor-raised' status, plus an editable Core-floor control — matching the user-approved mock at mocks/model-tiers-grouped.html. It reads and writes the same insrc.models.* configuration keys the native settings page already uses; no new config keys are introduced. Non-goal: the mock's 'Check an unlisted model…' link is NOT implemented by this Story — that capability continues to be reached only through the existing 'insrc: Set model tier' QuickPick wizard's checkUnlisted flow (model-tier-picker.ts:360-449), which this Story leaves untouched.

hldContextSlice.frameworkSummary: Standalone feature — no parent HLD. Design directly against the repo, grounded on the s1 analyze passes. There are no HLD shared contracts to honour.

boundary.internal: Group the VS Code Model Tiers settings by tier instead of 9 flat fields

api.name: currentTier
api.signature: export function currentTier(defs: ModelDefinitions, raw: Record<string, unknown>, tier: Tier): TierValue | undefined

parameters.name: defs
parameters.purpose: the daemon's model catalog, used to resolve the stored runner/model strings into a typed value

parameters.name: raw
parameters.purpose: the plugin's current insrc.models.* configuration snapshot

returns.meaning: the tier's current runner/model/effort as configured, or undefined if unset

preconditions: raw is the plugin's own machine-scope insrc.models.* configuration snapshot, not arbitrary JSON
postconditions: does not mutate defs or raw
visibility changes from private (vscode-plugin/src/models/model-tier-picker.ts:149) to exported; no signature or behavior change

api.name: tierStatus
api.signature: export function tierStatus(defs: ModelDefinitions, raw: Record<string, unknown>, tier: Tier, coreFloor: Tier): TierStatus

parameters.name: defs
parameters.purpose: the daemon's model catalog, used to classify whether the configured model is still listed/supported

parameters.name: raw
parameters.purpose: the plugin's current insrc.models.* configuration snapshot

parameters.name: coreFloor
parameters.purpose: the resolved insrc.models.coreFloor setting, used to detect when this tier is raised

returns.meaning: one of ok | not-supported | not-listed | floor-raised for this tier

postconditions: returns 'floor-raised' only when tier ranks below coreFloor among core > mid > cheap

classifies a configured-but-unresolved model: family.host is set only for the family whose CLI runs on a host such as Ollama with a closed model list (vscode-plugin/src/models/definitions.ts:32-33); when familyOf(defs, configured runner) resolves to such a family, returns 'not-supported' (a closed list can't fall back); when it resolves to an open vendor family (host undefined, e.g. claude/codex), returns 'not-listed' (runs the default) — the same two-way split pickModel's inline marker already applies at vscode-plugin/src/models/model-tier-picker.ts:335-339

additionally classifies the case pickModel's marker does not cover: when the configured runner itself does not resolve to any family in defs (an unknown/stale runner), tierStatus reports 'not-listed' directly from that unresolved lookup, rather than through currentTier's fallback (vscode-plugin/src/models/model-tier-picker.ts:149-165), which silently substitutes the default family's value for that case and would otherwise lose the distinction

api.name: renderModelTiers

parameters.name: deps
parameters.purpose: injected modelDefinitions + rawConfig the renderer reads from

returns.meaning: a () => Promise<string> thunk the panel host calls to (re)render the webview body, mirroring RepoConfigRenderer's shape (vscode-plugin/src/panels/repo-config.ts:82)

preconditions: deps.modelDefinitions and deps.rawConfig reflect the current model catalog and insrc.models.* settings at render time
postconditions: returned HTML embeds one card per tier built from currentTier + tierStatus, plus the mock's panel-foot Core-floor <select> bound to the current insrc.models.coreFloor value, matching mocks/model-tiers-grouped.html

does NOT render the mock's panel-foot 'Check an unlisted model…' link — out of scope for this Story (non-goal; see Summary); that affordance remains reachable only via the existing 'insrc: Set model tier' QuickPick wizard's checkUnlisted flow

api.name: createModelTiersWriteHandler
api.signature: export function createModelTiersWriteHandler(deps: ModelTiersWriteHandlerDeps): (write: ModelTiersWrite) => void

parameters.name: deps
parameters.purpose: injected config-write + refresh callback, mirroring RepoConfigWriteDeps (vscode-plugin/src/panels/repo-config.ts:40)

returns.meaning: a handler the panel host forwards every incoming ModelTiersWrite message to, mirroring createRepoConfigWriteHandler's shape (vscode-plugin/src/panels/repo-config.ts:174)

errors.condition: the daemon's config.write call rejects (a thrown/caught error, e.g. daemon unreachable); handled the same way createRepoConfigWriteHandler's catch block already handles it (repo-config.ts:220-222) — logs via deps.logger and does NOT call deps.refresh()

preconditions: write.kind === 'tierField' addresses an existing insrc.models.tiers.<tier>.<field> key (vscode-plugin/package.json:360-432); write.kind === 'coreFloor' addresses the existing insrc.models.coreFloor key — no new keys are introduced
postconditions: when config.write RESOLVES (whether the daemon accepts or refuses the write), calls deps.refresh() unconditionally, exactly as createRepoConfigWriteHandler's deps.refresh() call (repo-config.ts:219) runs on both an accepted and a refused resolution

when config.write instead REJECTS (throws), logs the failure and does NOT call deps.refresh() — the panel keeps showing its last-rendered (pre-write) state until the next natural re-render, exactly as createRepoConfigWriteHandler's catch branch (repo-config.ts:220-222) behaves on a rejection

api.name: openModelTiers

returns.meaning: opens/reveals the singleton Model Tiers panel; if deps.modelTiersRenderer is unset, renders a placeholder body instead of the real cards

postconditions: always opens/reveals the panel, exactly as openRepoConfiguration unconditionally does (vscode-plugin/src/panels/webview-host.ts:398-415) — it is never a no-op
when deps.modelTiersRenderer is unset, shows a static placeholder body (mirroring REPO_PLACEHOLDER, webview-host.ts:293-313) instead of the rendered cards
panel content reflects the latest rawConfig/modelDefinitions at the moment it's called, when a renderer is present
new method on WebviewPanelHost (vscode-plugin/src/panels/types.ts:34), implemented in webview-host.ts alongside the existing openRepoConfiguration

dataModelChanges.details: type TierStatus = { kind: 'ok' } | { kind: 'floor-raised'; to: Tier } | { kind: 'not-supported'; model: string } | { kind: 'not-listed'; model: string }. Generalizes pickModel's existing inline marker text into a reusable value.
interface ModelTiersRendererDeps { modelDefinitions: ModelDefinitions; rawConfig: Record<string, unknown>; }. Narrower analog of RepoConfigRendererDeps (vscode-plugin/src/panels/types.ts:186-193).

type ModelTiersWrite = { kind: 'tierField'; tier: Tier; field: 'runner' | 'model' | 'effort'; value: string } | { kind: 'coreFloor'; value: Tier }. Covers both editable controls in the approved mock (mocks/model-tiers-grouped.html:96-157 per-tier dropdowns, :160-166 the panel-foot Core-floor <select>); structurally a discriminated-union widening of the single-shape RepoConfigWrite (vscode-plugin/src/panels/types.ts:202-206), needed because this panel writes two distinct config paths (insrc.models.tiers.<tier>.<field> and insrc.models.coreFloor) where Repo Configuration only ever writes one shape.
interface mirroring RepoConfigWriteDeps (vscode-plugin/src/panels/repo-config.ts:40): carries the daemon config.write call and a refresh(): void callback.
adds modelTiersRenderer?: ModelTiersRenderer | undefined and onModelTiersWrite?: ((write: ModelTiersWrite) => void) | undefined.
adds method openModelTiers(): void alongside the existing openRepoConfiguration(): void.
widens action: 'detailed' | 'repoConfig' to 'detailed' | 'repoConfig' | 'modelTiers', and the status-bar menu array gains a { label: 'Model Tiers', action: 'modelTiers' } entry.

errorCases.scenario: The daemon's config.write call rejects (throws) — daemon unreachable / IPC error — while saving a tier field or coreFloor change from the panel.
errorCases.detection: createModelTiersWriteHandler's call to config.write throws, caught in the handler's own try/catch, mirroring createRepoConfigWriteHandler's catch block (repo-config.ts:220-222).
errorCases.response: The handler logs the failure via its injected deps.logger and does NOT call deps.refresh() — the same as the cited catch block, which only logs.
errorCases.userImpact: The panel keeps showing its last-rendered (pre-write) state; the control the user just changed may visually disagree with the unwritten config until the panel is next reopened or manually refreshed. No silent data loss, but no inline error toast (consistent with the existing Repo Configuration write path).

errorCases.scenario: The daemon's config.write call resolves but REFUSES the write (e.g. a consent/validation refusal inside the daemon, result.ok === false) while saving a tier field or coreFloor change.
errorCases.detection: createModelTiersWriteHandler's call to config.write resolves with { ok: false, reason }.
errorCases.response: The handler calls deps.refresh() unconditionally on this resolution, exactly as createRepoConfigWriteHandler's deps.refresh() call (repo-config.ts:219) runs on both an accepted and a refused resolution.
errorCases.userImpact: The panel immediately re-renders from the daemon's current (still unwritten) config, so the control reverts to its last-known-good value.

errorCases.scenario: modelDefinitions is stale or empty (daemon model catalog not yet loaded) when the panel renders, so the configured runner does not resolve to any family.
errorCases.detection: tierStatus's own familyOf(defs, configured runner) lookup returns undefined, independent of currentTier's fallback (which would otherwise silently substitute the default family).
errorCases.response: tierStatus reports 'not-listed' directly from the unresolved lookup.
errorCases.userImpact: User sees an accurate 'not served by X' warning instead of a blank panel.

errorCases.scenario: A webview postMessage arrives with a malformed ModelTiersWrite, e.g. from a stale webview script version.
errorCases.detection: The host's onMessage handler validates the message shape before forwarding: for a tier-field write, type === 'modelTiersWrite', kind === 'tierField', tier one of 'core'|'mid'|'cheap', field one of 'runner'|'model'|'effort', value a string; for a core-floor write, kind === 'coreFloor' and value one of 'core'|'mid'|'cheap' — mirroring handleRepoMessage's existing repoWrite shape validation (webview-host.ts:322-333).
errorCases.response: A message that fails this check is silently dropped (no-op) and never reaches onModelTiersWrite, exactly as an unrecognized message is today (webview-host.ts:371, 'Anything else is a silent no-op').
errorCases.userImpact: No write occurs for a malformed message; the panel's displayed state is unaffected.

edgeCases.input: All three tiers configured identically (same runner/model/effort).
edgeCases.expected: Three distinct cards are still rendered, each independently editable; no dedup logic is applied.

edgeCases.input: A tier's configured model has been removed from the catalog entirely.
edgeCases.expected: tierStatus returns not-supported; the dropdown shows the removed model styled distinctly with effort disabled, matching mocks/model-tiers-grouped.html.

edgeCases.input: insrc.models.coreFloor is set to 'cheap' (the lowest tier).
edgeCases.expected: tierStatus never returns floor-raised for any tier; the floor-badge is omitted from all three cards.

edgeCases.input: User changes the panel-foot Core-floor dropdown to a different tier.
edgeCases.expected: A { kind: 'coreFloor', value } ModelTiersWrite is posted; createModelTiersWriteHandler writes insrc.models.coreFloor and the panel re-renders with the new floor-raised badges applied to the appropriate tier(s).

edgeCases.input: User changes the same dropdown twice in quick succession before the first config.write resolves.
edgeCases.expected: Each ModelTiersWrite is forwarded and handled independently in arrival order; this Story adds no debouncing.

invariantsToPreserve.text: The Model Tiers panel reads and writes only the existing insrc.models.tiers.<tier>.<field> and insrc.models.coreFloor keys; no new configuration keys are introduced.

currentTier's resolution behavior is unchanged by exporting it; the existing 'insrc: Set model tier' QuickPick wizard (runSetModelTier) continues to work identically.
